headline: Tk 6,000 fine: Minister's car booked for wrong-side driving in Dhaka
summary: Police filed two cases against a Range Rover belonging to the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism while Minister Rashiduzzaman Millat was inside.
details: Police filed two cases against a Range Rover belonging to the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism after it was found travelling on the wrong side of Circuit House Road in Dhaka this morning.
The vehicle, bearing registration number Dhaka Metro-Gha-18-2125, was stopped at around 9:08am as it was heading towards the Secretariat on the wrong side of the road.
The driver, Arif Hossain, was fined Tk 6,000 in total—Tk 3,000 for each of the two offences, including reckless driving.
Minister Rashiduzzaman Millat was inside the vehicle when it was stopped by the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's traffic division.

Traffic officials described the action as unprecedented, noting they could not recall any previous instance in Bangladesh where a case was filed against a minister's vehicle for driving on the wrong side of the road.
Senior police officials stated that the action serves as a message that traffic rules apply equally to everyone, regardless of the status of the passengers.
caption:

Police filed two cases against a Range Rover belonging to the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism after it was found travelling on the wrong side of Circuit House Road in Dhaka this morning.

The vehicle, bearing registration number Dhaka Metro-Gha-18-2125, was stopped at around 9:08am as it was heading towards the Secretariat on the wrong side of the road.

The driver, Arif Hossain, was fined Tk 6,000 in total—Tk 3,000 for each of the two offences, including reckless driving.

Minister Rashiduzzaman Millat was inside the vehicle when it was stopped by the Dhaka Metropolitan Police's traffic division.

Traffic officials described the action as unprecedented, noting they could not recall any previous instance in Bangladesh where a case was filed against a minister's vehicle for driving on the wrong side of the road.

Senior police officials stated that the action serves as a message that traffic rules apply equally to everyone, regardless of the status of the passengers.

headline_marked: Global prices, gas crisis: [[Commerce Minister explains oil and sugar price hikes]]
headline: Global prices, gas crisis: Commerce Minister explains oil and sugar price hikes
summary: Minister Khandakar Abdul Muqtadir says edible oil prices rose due to global market trends, while sugar production is hit by gas supply disruptions.
details: Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muqtadir stated that edible oil prices have increased in the local market to align with rising prices in the international market.
Regarding sugar, the Minister explained that disruptions in gas supply to refineries have caused temporary production issues, though sufficient raw sugar stocks are available.

Speaking at a policy dialogue on the leather sector in Dhaka, the Minister noted that commodity prices fluctuate due to global supply chain issues, crop failures, energy crises, or transport problems.
To combat inflation, the government is preparing to sell essential goods at low prices in every city corporation and district headquarters during the upcoming Ramadan.
The Minister also clarified that the new government employee pay scale will not cause further price hikes, as the salary adjustments are being implemented in phases after 11 years of inflation.
Addressing concerns over aromatic rice, he stated that only about 2,000 tonnes were exported, and the remaining approved export volume is being reduced to ensure local supply.
The government continues to monitor the market, including LC openings and shipping movements, to ensure adequate stocks of essential commodities.
caption:
Why are oil and sugar prices rising? The Commerce Minister breaks down the causes and the government's plan for Ramadan.

Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muqtadir stated that edible oil prices have increased in the local market to align with rising prices in the international market.

Regarding sugar, the Minister explained that disruptions in gas supply to refineries have caused temporary production issues, though sufficient raw sugar stocks are available.

Speaking at a policy dialogue on the leather sector in Dhaka, the Minister noted that commodity prices fluctuate due to global supply chain issues, crop failures, energy crises, or transport problems.

To combat inflation, the government is preparing to sell essential goods at low prices in every city corporation and district headquarters during the upcoming Ramadan.

The Minister also clarified that the new government employee pay scale will not cause further price hikes, as the salary adjustments are being implemented in phases after 11 years of inflation.

Addressing concerns over aromatic rice, he stated that only about 2,000 tonnes were exported, and the remaining approved export volume is being reduced to ensure local supply.

The government continues to monitor the market, including LC openings and shipping movements, to ensure adequate stocks of essential commodities.
